pages.text:
Maya’s school library was usually quiet. Children read books there. Mrs. Bell stamped cards there. Even the chairs made only tiny sounds.

But on Friday morning, the library looked different.

A big treasure map was pinned to the board. The bookshelves were drawn like mountains. The reading carpet was called Red Island. At the bottom of the map were big words:

Find the Golden Bookmark!

Mrs. Bell smiled. “Today, each team will follow the map and find the hidden bookmark.”

Everyone cheered.

Just then, a fat grey cat walked in through the open door. It jumped onto a chair, then onto the table, and sat proudly beside the treasure map.

“Whose cat is that?” asked Ben.

“He wants to win the prize!” said Lila.

Everyone laughed. Mrs. Bell gently picked up the cat. “Out you go, Captain Whiskers,” she said.

While everyone was laughing, Maya moved closer to the map. She wanted to see the path clearly. The dotted line went from Red Island to Shelf C, then toward the Whispering Corner.

Maya touched the corner of the map.

Suddenly, Captain Whiskers jumped back through the door and ran under the table. Maya stepped back quickly. Her hand pulled the paper.

Rrrrip!

A small corner of the map tore off.

Maya froze. The torn piece had part of the dotted path on it. No one had seen.

Mrs. Bell was busy chasing Captain Whiskers. Ben was laughing. Lila was clapping her hands.

Maya’s heart beat fast.

Mrs. Bell trusted me. Everyone will be upset.

So Maya folded the torn piece and pushed it into her pocket.

A minute later, Jonah walked near the map. Jonah was new in class. He was quiet and often stood alone.

Mrs. Bell came back and looked at the map. “Oh dear,” she said. “A corner is missing.”

Lila pointed at Jonah. “Jonah was just there.”

Jonah looked scared. “I didn’t touch it.”

Ben whispered, “Maybe he tore it.”

Maya looked down. The paper in her pocket felt heavy.

Mrs. Bell said, “No accusing. If someone knows what happened, please tell me.”

Maya wanted to speak. But she stayed quiet.

The treasure hunt began, but soon everyone got stuck.

“The path stops at Shelf C!” said Ben.

“We need the missing corner,” said Lila.

Jonah stood quietly near the wall. He did not look excited anymore.

Maya felt worse and worse.

Then Mrs. Bell said, “We may have to stop the hunt. It is not fair if the map is incomplete.”

Not fair.

Maya slowly took the paper from her pocket. “I have it,” she said softly.

Everyone looked at her.

“I tore it by mistake,” Maya said. “I got scared, so I hid it. Jonah did not do it.”

Jonah looked at Maya.

Maya said, “I’m sorry.”

Mrs. Bell did not shout. “Thank you for telling the truth,” she said. “Now please help repair the map.”

Maya taped the corner back. The map had a shiny tape line, but everyone could follow it again.

Jonah found the next clue behind the poetry shelf.

“I found it!” he said happily.

This time, everyone smiled at him.

Maya did not win the prize. But when she touched her pocket, it was empty.

And her heart felt light.
